blocks.emptyText: No scenarios yet — create your first plan.

blocks.value: Edit users, revenue and cost figures period by period. Year-1 rows are monthly; later rows are yearly.
New customers won each month, by segment. This is the one table in the revenue model you type into — everything else is derived from it.
Onboarding beyond the standard setup fee, custom development, consulting, white-label and marketplace. Kept out of the subscription line because none of it is recurring platform revenue.
Each segment described AT MATURITY. A customer arrives small and grows into these numbers along the adoption curve.

How much of a customer's eventual size is live at each age. One curve for every segment. Past month twelve it goes above 1.0 — a retained customer keeps growing, which is where most of the revenue comes from.
What each plan would cost this customer at this age, and therefore what they pay. The cheapest column wins — the plan is an outcome, not an assumption.
Base fee, rate per active user x app, and the cap factor k. Billable users for one app stop at k x the square root of the customer's active users.

entities.label: Scenario

blocks.value: A summary of what the other tabs say. Change a price in Pricing & Users, a cost in Costs & Fees or a role in Hiring, and every month recalculates.

fields.help: Number of months modelled monthly before the plan switches to yearly periods.
fields.label: Monthly Detail (months)
Total Plan Costs
fields.help: Cost of revenue, people and operating costs across every period.

fields.label: Cash At Plan End
fields.help: Opening cash plus everything the periods moved — the same number the last period's Cash at end shows.

fields.label: Runway (months)
fields.help: Months of cover at the plan's average monthly spend.

fields.label: Plan months
fields.help: How many monthly periods to generate for this plan

fields.label: Fixed costs / month
fields.help: Summary of the Costs & Fees tab. Change it there.

fields.label: Revenue-share fees
fields.help: Summary of the Costs & Fees tab. Change it there.

fields.label: One-off costs
fields.help: Summary of the Costs & Fees tab. Change it there.

fields.label: AI billed to customers
fields.help: Share of recurring MRR billed on for AI. The workbook carries 6% as a COST; billing it on at the same rate is pure pass-through.

fields.label: Provider discount
fields.help: How much less we pay the provider than we bill. This is the AI margin: we ask the customer a published rate and may buy cheaper.

entities.description: One named version of the budget plan (e.g. Conservative, Base, Optimistic) that everything else hangs off.

entities.label: Plan

fields.label: Base fee / month
fields.help: Charged whatever the usage is. Zero on Flex.

fields.label: Rate / active user x app
fields.help: One unit is one person actively using one shared app this month.

fields.label: Cap factor k
fields.help: Billable users for ONE app stop at k x the square root of the customer's active users. Blank on Flex (no cap) and on Enterprise (negotiated).

entities.description: One row of the published price list: a base fee, a rate per active user x app, and the cap factor k. Nothing here says who buys it — a customer lands on whichever plan is cheapest for their shape, so the plan is an outcome.

entities.label: Adoption Point
entities.description: One month of the universal adoption curve: how much of a customer's eventual size is live at that age. The same curve applies to every segment, which is what makes it one editable assumption rather than three.

fields.label: Platform user adoption
fields.help: Share of the segment's mature active users live at this age. Passes 1.0 after month 12 — a retained customer keeps growing.

fields.label: Shared apps adoption
fields.help: Share of the segment's mature shared-app count live at this age.

entities.label: Segment
entities.description: A band of company size, described at MATURITY. A customer arrives small and grows into these numbers along the adoption curve.

fields.label: Mature active users
fields.help: Active Cordango users in the company once it is fully rolled out. This is N in the cap formula.

fields.label: Average app adoption
fields.help: Share of the company's active users who use any ONE given app. Multiplied by active users to get A, the per-app population the cap bounds.

fields.label: Setup / services fee
fields.help: One-off, invoiced in the month the customer is won.

fields.label: Churn / month
fields.help: Applied as pow(1 - rate, age - 1) along the cohort. The workbook defines this per segment and never applies it; here it does.

entities.label: Lifecycle Step
entities.description: One segment at one age: how big the customer is, what each plan would cost them, and therefore what they pay. The cheapest plan wins, so this row is where a plan stops being an assumption.

fields.label: Shared apps
fields.help: Never below one: a customer with no shared app is not a customer.

fields.label: Flex would cost
fields.help: No base fee and no cap — every active user of every app is billed.

computed.expr: starter.monthly_base_fee + shared_apps * min(active_per_app, starter.cap_multiplier * pow(active_users, 0.5)) * starter.price_per_app_user
pro.monthly_base_fee + shared_apps * min(active_per_app, pro.cap_multiplier * pow(active_users, 0.5)) * pro.price_per_app_user
advanced.monthly_base_fee + shared_apps * min(active_per_app, advanced.cap_multiplier * pow(active_users, 0.5)) * advanced.price_per_app_user

fields.label: MRR (cheapest plan)
fields.help: The customer is not asked to choose badly. Which plan won is readable from the four columns beside this one — naming it would need a conditional the expression language does not have.

fields.label: Surviving share of the cohort
fields.help: pow(1 - churn, age - 1). Age one is a full cohort.

fields.label: MRR per customer won
fields.help: What one customer won at age zero is still paying at this age, churn already taken off. The grid multiplies this by the cohort size.

entities.label: Acquisition
entities.description: New customers won in one month, in one segment. This is the one table in the revenue model somebody types into.

fields.label: Plan month
fields.help: Counted from the plan start. Month 1 is the first month.

fields.label: New customers
fields.help: Typed. Everything downstream of it is derived.

fields.label: Setup & services
fields.help: Invoiced once, in the month the customers are won.

entities.label: Cohort Month
entities.description: One cohort at one age. The grid exists because a rollup can add a field up but cannot multiply two rows together, and month m's revenue is exactly that product summed over every live cohort.

fields.label: Lands in month
fields.help: The cohort's own month plus its age, less one. Two references, one hop each — which is the rule, and is what makes the grid legal.

entities.label: Period

fields.label: Tax provision
fields.help: Tax provision — a judgement, not a derivation

fields.label: Actual revenue
fields.help: What actually came in, once the month has closed

fields.label: Actual costs
fields.help: What actually went out, once the month has closed

fields.label: Actual customers
fields.help: Actual active users at month end

fields.label: People cost (loaded)
fields.help: Sum of the hiring lines covering this month, each already carrying its own employer cost rate. Nobody types this, and nothing adds a second burden on top.

fields.label: Total operating expenses
fields.help: Sum of the cost lines whose months cover this period — marketing, tooling, insurance, contingency, statutory fees. Nobody types this.

fields.label: Headcount
fields.help: Heads on the payroll this period.

fields.label: Active customers (exact)
fields.help: Carried to four places so churn stays visible on a small base. The whole-customer figure beside it is what people read.

fields.label: Active customers
fields.help: Whole companies. The fraction is carried in the exact figure beside this one and rounded once, here.

fields.label: One-off costs (dated)
fields.help: One-off payments dated inside this period — formation, equipment, statutory fees.

fields.label: Funding received
fields.help: Rounds closing inside this period. Money in, so it lifts the cash line.

computed.expr: opex_total + one_off_total + ai_cost + revenue_fees + payroll_fees + hiring_one_off

fields.label: Churned customers
fields.help: What the cohort decay took: last month's base plus this month's wins, less what is actually still here.

fields.label: Revenue-share rate
fields.help: Fees charged as a share of revenue, for the lines running this month.

fields.label: Hiring one-off costs
fields.help: Equipment and onboarding for the roles STARTING this month.

fields.label: Payroll-share rate
fields.help: Fees charged as a share of gross payroll — Berufsgenossenschaft and the like.

fields.label: One-off costs (by plan month)
fields.help: One-offs placed by plan month rather than by calendar date.

fields.label: Net cash movement
fields.help: Cash equals revenue in this version — the workbook's own simplification. Annual prepayment is a later slice.

fields.label: Recurring MRR
fields.help: Every live cohort at its own age. The number no single expression can reach, which is what the cohort grid is for.

fields.label: Enterprise MRR (manual)
fields.help: Negotiated deal by deal, so there is no per-customer price to derive it from. Typed, like the workbook's own column.

entities.description: One modelled period of a scenario (month in year 1, then year): users, revenue, costs and cash.

entities.label: Team

fields.help: Typical gross annual salary for a hire in this team; prefilled onto new hiring lines.
fields.label: Default Gross Salary / Year

entities.description: A functional team hiring is grouped by (Engineering, Sales, ...).

entities.label: Hiring Line

fields.help: Leave empty for an open-ended role.
fields.label: Planned End

fields.help: German employer social contributions on top of gross (approx. 20-22%).
fields.label: Employer Cost Rate

fields.help: Equipment, tooling, recruiting fee amortised per head per year.
fields.label: Other Cost per Head / Year
One-off Cost per Head
fields.help: Equipment, recruiter fee and onboarding — charged once, in the month the role starts.

entities.description: Planned headcount for a team from a given start month, with salary and employer costs.

entities.label: Cost Line

fields.help: Used when behaviour is Fixed monthly.
fields.label: Fixed Amount / Month

fields.help: Used when behaviour is Per user.
fields.label: Amount per User / Month

fields.help: Used when behaviour is One-off.
fields.label: One-off Amount

fields.help: Trade register, IHK, notary, Finanzamt, GmbH filing and similar German statutory costs.
fields.label: Government / Statutory Fee
Percent of Revenue
fields.help: Used when behaviour is % of revenue — payment and collection fees, revenue share, affiliate commission.

fields.label: Percentage Of
fields.help: Which figure the percentage applies to. Both are always positive, so the fee can never come out as a credit.

fields.label: One-off Month
fields.help: Month of the plan this is paid, counting from month 1. Use this OR the exact date, whichever you actually know.

entities.description: A non-payroll cost: fixed monthly, scaling per user, or a one-off payment such as a German government fee.

entities.label: Revenue Stream
entities.description: Revenue that is not the subscription: onboarding and migration, custom app development, consulting, white-label licensing, marketplace. Kept separate because none of it is recurring platform revenue.

fields.label: Amount / Month
fields.help: Used when behaviour is Recurring monthly.

fields.label: One-off Month
fields.help: Month of the plan this is invoiced, counting from month 1. Use this OR the exact date, whichever you actually know.

fields.label: Paid out to the creator
fields.help: Marketplace split. The working assumption is 20% to the app creator and 80% to Cordango, but it is not settled, so it is a number rather than a rule.

fields.label: Ends
fields.help: Leave empty for open-ended.

entities.label: Cost Category
entities.description: Lookup list grouping cost lines (Infrastructure, Software, Government fees, Office, Marketing...).

entities.label: Funding Round
entities.description: Money coming in from investors within a scenario.

entities.label: Assumption
entities.description: A named assumption behind a scenario's numbers, so investors can see what drives the plan.

entities.label: Planner Settings

fields.help: Employer social contributions on top of gross salary (Kranken-, Renten-, Arbeitslosen-, Pflegeversicherung, U1/U2).
fields.label: Default Employer Cost Rate

fields.help: Körperschaftsteuer + Solidaritätszuschlag + Gewerbesteuer combined.
fields.label: Corporate Tax Rate

entities.description: App-wide defaults for new scenarios and German employer cost rules.

archetype.coreJob: Build a multi-year budget plan per scenario — period by period revenue, headcount, costs, funding and runway — and compare scenarios for investors.

workflows.name: Start the scenario with a plan to edit

set.name: IHK contribution
set.notes: €180/year base band up to €30,700 trade income (Wirtschaftssatzung 2026). The bands step up to €900; raise this as the plan grows. The additional 0.25% levy applies to positive trade income only, so it is nil while the plan is loss-making.

set.name: Berufsgenossenschaft
set.notes: Planning rate of 1% of gross payroll. The real contribution depends on payroll, risk class and the tariff — confirm with the BG once registered.

set.name: Transparency register
set.notes: €19.80 a year under TrGebV, from fee year 2024.

set.name: Annual accounts & register filing
set.notes: €300/year planning reserve. Validate with your adviser or filing provider.

set.name: Other mandatory fees
set.notes: €500/year reserve — bank confirmations, extracts, licences and small charges.

set.name: Founding equipment
set.notes: Laptops, test devices and office equipment.

set.name: Vertical GTM experiments
set.notes: Ten brands/landing pages, demos and initial creative tests.

set.name: Security & architecture review
set.notes: External review before broader customer onboarding.

description: Build and maintain an investor-ready financial budget plan: named scenarios, a usage-based price list (base fee plus active user x app, capped), customer growth and churn, monthly and yearly projections with recognized revenue and cash collected side by side, hiring by team, cost lines, services revenue, funding rounds, cash balance and runway.
